setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step melody on the example MIDI device: trigs on steps 1 to 4 on pattern degrees 1 to 4 of scale slot 1 (C major), so MIDI 60, 62, 64 and 65. Global transposition is 0, playback is stopped and the norns shows the Device page.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Press Scale (4,8) to open the Scale Editor, then tap Play (1,8). One step lasts about a sixth of a second at 90 BPM, so the four-note phrase repeats about every two thirds of a second; exact timing does not matter. While it loops, press (16,8) on the transposition fader once. The screen shows Scale overview with Transpose +1: the note sounding at that moment keeps its pitch and length, and the next notes play a semitone higher, MIDI 61, 63, 65 and 66, as the MIDI strip lists.
steps.title: Press +1 while it plays

steps.caption: After a few more notes press (9,8) to set -12. Transpose reads -12: again the sounding note is untouched and the next notes drop an octave below the written pitches, 48, 50, 52 and 53.
steps.title: Press -12 a few notes later

steps.caption: Tap Play to stop. Transpose still reads -12, and in the strip every note-on has its own matching note-off.
steps.title: Stop

steps.caption: Both edits changed only the next onset: the notes before the first edit are 60, 62, 64, 65, then 61, 63, 65, 66, then 48, 50, 52, 53, and each held note finished at its own pitch and length.
steps.title: The whole run
